However, they rely on assumptions of local continuity that often fail in recursive, self-modulating cognitive architectures.</jats:p>\\n                  </jats:sec>\\n                  <jats:sec>\\n                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>\\n                    <jats:p>We analyze the limitations of local proxy models through formal reasoning, simulation experiments, and epistemological framing. We introduce constructs such as Modular Cognitive Attention (MCA), the Cognitive Leap Operator (Ψ), and the Internal Narrative Generator (ING).</jats:p>\\n                  </jats:sec>\\n                  <jats:sec>\\n                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>\\n                    <jats:p>Our findings show that local perturbations yield divergent interpretive outcomes depending on internal cognitive states. Narrative coherence emerges from recursive policy dynamics, and traditional attribution methods fail to capture bifurcation points in decision space.</jats:p>\\n                  </jats:sec>\\n                  <jats:sec>\\n                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>\\n                    <jats:p>We argue for a shift from post-hoc local approximations to embedded narrative-based interpretability. This reframing supports epistemic transparency in future AGI systems and aligns with cognitive theories of understanding.</jats:p>\\n                  </jats:sec>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.3389/frai.2025.1677528\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 12, 1]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1126/aaas.adf0782\", \"title\": [\"Artificial Intelligence and the Courts: Artificial Intelligence - Foundational Issues and Glossary\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1126/aaas.adf0782\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\…

This reframing supports epistemic transparency in future AGI systems and aligns with cognitive theories of understanding.</jats:p>\\n                  </jats:sec>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.3389/frai.2025.1677528\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 12, 1]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1126/aaas.adf0782\", \"title\": [\"Artificial Intelligence and the Courts: Artificial Intelligence - Foundational Issues and Glossary\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1126/aaas.adf0782\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2022, 9, 29]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1093/oso/9780198870944.003.0005\", \"title\": [\"Foundational Patents in Artificial Intelligence\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>\\n               <jats:p>Despite advocating openness, technology leaders have been patenting artificial intelligence (AI) inventions at an exponentially increasing rate. Patents on foundational techniques with broad applications have the potential to deter innovation in the field, should the privatization of key components of artificial intelligence be used to exclude third-party innovators. This chapter studies patent applications in the US and demonstrates the extent to which the field has grown over the last twenty years. It then seeks to explore foundational patents by focusing on triadic patents: patents filed jointly with the United States Patent and Trademark Office, the European Patent Office, and the Japanese Patent Office. The results of this chapter indicate an increasingly globalized AI field. A proverbial land grab seems to be occurring; an increase in AI patenting, particularly the protection of triadic patents, illustrates industry players aggressively attempting to own the building blocks of a rapidly emerging market. A number of policy levers are presented, highlighting how the patent offices and courts can counter the patenting of foundational patents by relying on strict and narrow patentability standards.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1093/oso/9780198870944.003.0005\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2021, 2, 25]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1016/s0004-3702(97)00047-7\", \"title\": [\"Axioms of causal relevance\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1016/s0004-3702(97)00047-7\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[1997, 12]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "be621bd2dcab371bb44cbfb45ba22ea9e317e29dd88076535054760087254ca9", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "assumption_challenge", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.3389/frai.2025.1677528", "doi:10.1126/aaas.adf0782", "doi:10.1093/oso/9780198870944.003.0005", "doi:10.1016/s0004-3702(97)00047-7"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.3389/frai.2025.1677528", "https://doi.org/10.1126/aaas.adf0782", "https://doi.org/10.1093/oso/9780198870944.003.0005", "https://doi.org/10.1016/s0004-3702(97)00047-7"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
